tier_reason: First-party numbers only: the README's '1,000 times faster than ptrace' has no timing at all, while Documentation/README.md gives a getpid hook-overhead comparison with ASC-Hook (14 ns against 39 ns, LD_PRELOAD 3 ns) and an initial-setup comparison (25 ms against 1890 ms) on a stated HoneyComb LX2 (NXP LX2160A Cortex-A72) running Linux 5.10, but the getpid microbenchmark code is not in the repository and no compiler or flags are given. The Middleware 2025 paper (peer-reviewed) could not be opened (dl.acm.org blocked, no mirror found), so it cannot lift the tier to B yet.

corrections.baseline: ptrace-based system call interception (README headline, no numbers); ASC-Hook, another ARM64 binary-rewriting syscall hook (Documentation/README.md, with numbers)
corrections.claimed_speedup: README Key Features: '1,000 times faster than `ptrace`', with no ptrace timing anywhere in the repository. Documentation/README.md 'Overhead Comparision with ASC-Hook': time to hook getpid is 14 ns for svc-hook, 39 ns for ASC-Hook and 3 ns for plain LD_PRELOAD, so the trampoline overhead is 11 ns against 36 ns (about 3.3x, derived from page data); initial setup takes 25 ms against 1890 ms for ASC-Hook ('75 times faster'). The same page reports the cost of hooking against unhooked runs: SQLite per-operation time up 0.01% to 2.6%, PostgreSQL 17.6 pgbench 10790 TPS hooked against 10923 TPS unhooked (1.2% reduction), Samba 4.15 throughput down 0.9% (download, 647 to 641 MB/s) and 0.1% (upload, 858 to 857 MB/s).
corrections.caveats: Category fit is weak: syscall-interception tooling built on instruction rewriting, not an assembler or disassembler, and neither ptrace nor ASC-Hook is GNU as, NASM or MASM. The 1,000x ptrace figure is one README bullet with no method, hardware, kernel or command and no ptrace number exists on any repo page. The ASC-Hook numbers are first-party and say only that the setup is 'exactly same with the experiment mentioned in the section 4.1 in our paper'; the getpid microbenchmark is not in the repository and no compiler or flags are stated (hardware for the Documentation experiments: HoneyComb LX2, NXP LX2160A 16-core Cortex-A72 up to 2.2 GHz, 64 GB, Linux 5.10, glibc 2.31). Results 'reflect the implementation state at the time this document was committed' (Dec 2025); NetBSD support and trampoline-allocation changes landed in Aug 2026. The Middleware 2025 paper (Moroo, Tazaki, Yasukata, pages 195-201) was not opened (dl.acm.org blocked). Same research group as zpoline (ARM64 counterpart, separate code base, not a duplicate). Needs GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.rtld.seal=0 on glibc with memory sealing, procfs on FreeBSD/NetBSD and PaX mprotect disabled on NetBSD. Language inferred from main.c and the Makefile because the repo page shows no language bar.

notes: Record is accurate on the ptrace claim (no numbers) but missed the only head-to-head comparison in the repo: Documentation/README.md measures svc-hook against ASC-Hook (getpid hook 14 ns vs 39 ns, setup 25 ms vs 1890 ms), so baseline, benchmark_url and claimed_speedup were corrected. Shortcomings to record: ptrace 1,000x is an unmeasured README bullet; getpid benchmark code absent and compiler flags unstated; weak fit for assemblers-and-asm-tooling. Paper-access retier candidate (Middleware 2025) if dl.acm.org becomes reachable.

tier_reason: The repo's Documentation/README.md gives first-party per-getpid hook overheads (zpoline 41 ns from paper Table 1, later 10 ns; Intel Pin 2703 ns minus 74 ns kernel time) with only 'our hardware' as the machine, and the README's 100x ptrace claim has no numbers. The getpid benchmark and a gcc -O3 ptrace tracer were posted by the author in issue #10 (Nov 2023), but no CPU model or full flags are stated, so not A; the USENIX ATC 2023 paper (peer-reviewed; abstract snippet: '28.1~761.0 times lower overhead compared to existing mechanisms which ensure exhaustive hooking') could not be opened, so B is not reached yet.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: '100 times faster than ptrace.' (no numbers on the page). Documentation/README.md (USENIX ATC 2023 reviews Q&A, May 2023): zpoline hook overhead 41 ns (paper Table 1) against 2629 ns for the Intel Pin 3.27 System Call API (2703 ns per getpid minus 74 ns for the kernel getpid), about 64x (derived from page data); the reviewer-suggested short-jump variant gave 31 ns; the later 0xeb 0x6a 0x90 trampoline (May 2023) gave 10 ns, '4 times faster than the previous version'. Paper abstract (WebSearch snippet only, paper not opened): '28.1~761.0 times lower overhead compared to existing mechanisms which ensure exhaustive hooking'.
corrections.caveats: Category fit is weak: this is syscall-interception tooling built on instruction rewriting, not an assembler or disassembler, and the baselines (ptrace, Intel Pin) are not GNU as, NASM or MASM. The 100x headline has no table, hardware, kernel version or compiler flags on the README page. The 41 ns, 2629 ns and 10 ns figures come from the repo's Documentation page and quote the paper's Table 1 (paper not opened: usenix.org is not reachable here); the CPU is only called 'our hardware'. The 64x ratio mixes the paper's zpoline run with a Pin run done later for the reviews, possibly on different days. The getpid benchmark program is not in the repository; the author posted it and a PTRACE_SYSCALL-based tracer (compiled with gcc -O3, run with 1000 iterations against 100000 for the zpoline run) in issue #10 in November 2023, and the hook returns a dummy value without entering the kernel; setup time (trampoline, rewriting, dlmopen) is excluded from the overhead. Requires /proc/sys/vm/mmap_min_addr set to 0 (trampoline at virtual address 0, which weakens NULL-dereference protection; SELinux may also need disabling). The code is Apache-2.0 but links binutils libopcodes (GPL-3.0) for disassembly. The last commit is from January 2025.

notes: Record is accurate; claimed_speedup and caveats extended with the paper-abstract snippet and the issue #10 benchmark programs (getpid loop and ptrace tracer, gcc -O3). Shortcomings to record: 100x ptrace headline unmeasured on repo pages, Pin comparison measured separately from the paper's zpoline run, CPU unstated, mmap_min_addr=0 requirement, GPL-3.0 libopcodes link dependency, weak category fit. Paper-access retier candidate to B (USENIX ATC 2023 best paper, usenix.org blocked here).
